question.leadin: This ruler bore Caesarion while serving as Julius Caesar's mistress.
question.text: Who is this female Egyptian pharaoh from the Ptolemy dynasty who notably killed herself with a snakebite?
question.clue: Drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar apocryphally won a bet for this ruler, whose short-lived successor was Caesarion.

swap.leadin: This son of Akhenaten ruled with the assistance of the vizier Ay ("eye"), who eventually succeeded him after his death.
swap.text: Name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt, whose tomb was famously discovered nearly intact by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: One of this ruler's names which invoked the god Aten was changed after his "Restoration" reversed his probable father's monotheism.

question.leadin: This ruler's capital at Amarna was discovered by Flinders Petrie, and his wife was Nefertiti.
question.text: Name this 18th dynasty pharaoh who attempted to establish monotheistic sun worship.
question.clue: Like his father, who married a non-royal woman named Tiy, he married a woman who was not of royal blood, the daughter of a vizier named Ay.

swap.text: This young pharaoh, the son of Akhenaten, had his tomb excavated by Howard Carter.
swap.clue: George Herbert financed a mission in the Valley of the Kings that stumbled upon the resting place of this Pharaoh, son of Akhenaten.

question.text: This pharaoh of the Old Kingdom is most famous for ordering his architect Hemon to begin the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
question.clue: Flinders Petrie discovered the only three-dimensional depiction of this ruler, a small ivory statuette.

swap.text: This pharaoh of the Third Dynasty is most well-known for building a Step Pyramid at Saqqara, which was the first large fully stone building in Egypt. He also subdued the Sinai.
swap.clue: An official of this pharaoh communes with the god Khnum to stop a seven-year flood, as recorded on the Famine Stela.

question.leadin: George Cecil Ives founded an "Order" named for this city's greatest defeat, which is commemorated by a statue of a lion.
question.text: Name this city state that employed an elite military unit of 300 homosexual lovers known as its "Sacred Band."
question.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

swap.text: Ships traveling long distances in the ancient world stopped at the Himyarite site of Muza on this body of water. The Aksumite kingdom also used their papyrus-sailed ships to guard ports on this sea.
swap.clue: The kingdoms of Saba' and Himyar exported frankincense and myrrh ("murr") to the Roman Empire through this sea, whose western coastline was also home to the kingdom of Axum.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Ancient Egyptian agriculture.
question.text: Irrigation canals were dug in order to control and store the water generated from this annual event. Egyptians would plant their crops in October after the end of this event.
question.answerHtml: flooding of the Nile [or obvious equivalents indicating the overflow or inundation of the Nile River; prompt on floods]

swap.text: The Story of Sinuhe ("sin-NOO-hay") references the murder of Amenemhat I, a ruler of this Egyptian kingdom that ruled between the first two Intermediate Periods.
swap.clue: The fnal rulers of this period were called the Xois Dynasty since they moved the capital there.

question.leadin: The word aamu may refer to these people during their early contacts.
question.text: Name these people who invaded Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period. These people, who introduced the chariot to Egypt, constituted Egypt's Fifteenth Dynasty.
question.clue: In a satirical story, a ruler of these people complains that he can't sleep because of noisy hippos in a letter addressed to Seqenenre ("sek-en-EN-ray") Tao.

swap.text: In a Middle Kingdom "tale" titled for this profession, a serpent recounts how a flaming star killed 74 members of his kin. That serpent, who is the Lord of Punt, discusses bravery with a member of this profession.
swap.answerHtml: sailor [or al-Baḥriyy; accept The Story of the Shipwrecked Sailor; prompt on merchant]

question.text: The existence of this pharaoh is attested to by a namesake palette that depicts him with two crowns. This pharaoh was the unifier of Upper and Lower Egypt.
question.clue: This pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.

swap.leadin: Emperor Claudius wrote a letter to the inhabitants of a city in this province about Jewish freedom of worship.
swap.text: Name this region that became a Roman province a decade after its Queen Arsinoe was executed in Rome.
swap.clue: By the 1st century C.E. this province produced the largest share of the cura annonae.

question.leadin: One of these structures at Navesink ("nav-eh-sink") was the first US site to test an invention of Augustin-Jean Fresnel ("oh-GU-stin zhean fruh-NELL") because it was too big for the influential octagonal one of these structures at nearby Sandy Hook.
question.text: Name these structures. John McComb Jr. designed the first federal works project, one of these structures in Virginia.
question.answerHtml: lighthouse [or Sandy Hook Lighthouse or Navesink Twin Lights or Cape Henry Lighthouses]
question.clue: The design for these structures was improved again by Robert Stevenson, grandfather of author Robert Louis Stevenson.

swap.leadin: Herodotus claimed the thickness of Egyptian skulls at this battle was explained by not wearing turbans, and noted that Polycrates of Samos sent forty warships of unreliable scoundrels to take part.
swap.text: Name this 525 BC battle in which the Egyptian Psamtik III fell after the Greek general Phanes directed the Persians to some Arabs who helped them cross the Sinai desert.

question.text: The pyramid at el-Lahun, or Kahun, was designed for the second pharaoh of this name, who also built a great dike there. Except for its last female ruler Sobekneferu, the entire Twelfth Dynasty consisted only of pharaohs with this name or Amenemhat.
question.clue: This name of three Twelfth Dynasty pharaohs. Herodotus gave this name's Greek equivalent to a pharaoh who supposedly erected genitalia-topped columns to mock the cities he conquered in Asia Minor and Thrace.

swap.text: Little is known about him except for his Great Pyramid and the five boats buried next to it.
swap.clue: This pharaoh whose reign saw the construction of the first and largest pyramid at Giza.

question.text: Though most Egyptologists agree that ancient Egyptians were not black, they are certain that pharaohs from this dynasty were black. This last dynasty in the Third Intermediate Period lasted from 760 BC to 656 BC, and its fall marked the beginning of the Late Period.

swap.leadin: Critics of this historian claim that he has mis-interpreted a Ugaritic inscription to date a solar eclipse during the reign of Akhenaten to 1012 B.C.E, 350 years later than the conventional dating scheme.
swap.text: Name this Egyptologist and former rock musician who, in the book A Test of Time, put forth a highly controversial New Chronology which shifts the reigns of dozens of pharaohs forward by centuries.
